newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen range-bound, testing downside.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen range-bound, testing downside.

text.p: Japanese government bonds (JGBs) are expected to be mostly range-bound during Tokyo trading time on Thursday, albeit with a downward bias in the wake of the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey on Wednesday, which proved more positive than expected.

Statements from a senior BOJ official late Wednesday that Japan's economic recovery has not strengthened as much as the results of the tankan showed helped boost JGBs during overnight London trade, but profit-taking trimmed most of those gains.
A carry-over of London sentiment may spark initial short- covering in Tokyo, but profit-taking is expected to ensue.
"Moves in London showed us that profit-taking needs are quite strong, so gains in Tokyo are likely to be capped by that as well," one trust bank trader said.

But overall trade is expected to be range-bound, if edging lower, as operators sideline themselves ahead of Friday's release of key economic data, including May industrial production figures, due out at 0430 GMT.

One focus for the market will be the level at which institutional investors emerge to buy. Some buying by life insurers was detected on Wednesday, and this could well continue on Thursday, a different trust bank trader said.
Although the mood in the bond market is growing gradually more bearish, there are currently no factors strong enough to sell futures deeply into the 122-123 range, he added.
